I traced the root cause to load() in packages/opencode/src/config/agent.ts. For each agent file it calls ConfigParse.schema(), which throws on a schema mismatch. load() doesn't catch that error, so a single bad file makes the whole function throw and none of the agents load, not even the valid ones. Nothing higher up handles it either, so it reaches the startup config load and produces the "4 of 5 requests failed" error.

The loadMode() function right below it already does this the safe way. It uses Schema.decodeUnknownExit and Exit.isSuccess to skip a bad file instead of throwing. The one gap is that loadMode() skips silently, which is the agent-vs-mode inconsistency in #27133.

My plan is to align load() with loadMode() so an invalid file is skipped with a warning instead of crashing. That covers both #31481 and #27133. I'll leave ConfigParse.schema() itself alone, since throwing is the right behavior for a single config file.

I reproduced it on the current dev branch. Running load() against a folder with one valid agent and one Cursor-style agent (tools written as a YAML array) throws ConfigInvalidError. It happens in the shared config code, so it isn't tied to the terminal, OS, or frontend. Any invalid agent file triggers it. I'll open a PR shortly.

## Root cause found — closing as not-a-bug, but documenting for future reference

After further investigation, the real cause of my confusion was an environment variable in my shell, not a config-file issue.

### Two things are at play

1. **`MINIMAX_API_KEY` was set in my `~/.bashrc`** (line 192, `export MINIMAX_API_KEY=...`). opencode sees this env var and auto-enables the four built-in MiniMax providers (`minimax`, `minimax-cn`, `minimax-cn-coding-plan`, `minimax-coding-plan`) on every startup, regardless of what's in `auth.json` / `opencode.json`. `auth logout` only removes the credential, it does not clear the env var, so the providers get re-enabled on the next launch.

2. **`disabled_providers` in `opencode.json` does work for the CLI**, but is **not honored by the TUI model selector**. I verified this against the source:
   - `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts:1328,1331-1335,1549-1552` — the runtime provider loader builds `disabled = new Set(cfg.disabled_providers ?? [])` and removes matching providers.
   - `packages/opencode/test/provider/provider.test.ts` — there is even a test `"disabled_providers excludes provider"` confirming this works.
   - However, the TUI calls the server's `provider.list` endpoint (`packages/server/src/handlers/provider.ts`), which returns `catalog.provider.available()` from `packages/core/src/catalog.ts:224-229`. That method filters by `provider.enabled` only and **does not consult `disabled_providers` at all**. So even with `"disabled_providers": ["minimax", "minimax-cn"]` correctly loaded in the resolved config (verified with `opencode debug config`), the model selector still shows them.

   This second point is a real bug — `disabled_providers` is documented behavior and should be honored end-to-end. It is silently ignored in the TUI.

### Reproduction (local, v1.17.3)

```bash
$ opencode debug v2
Total providers: 9
  ...
  minimax: MiniMax (minimax.io) enabled={'via': 'env', 'name': 'MINIMAX_API_KEY'}
  minimax-cn: MiniMax (minimaxi.com) enabled={'via': 'env', 'name': 'MINIMAX_API_KEY'}
  minimax-cn-coding-plan: MiniMax Token Plan (minimaxi.com) enabled={'via': 'env', 'name': 'MINIMAX_API_KEY'}
  minimax-coding-plan: MiniMax Token Plan (minimax.io) enabled={'via': 'env', 'name': 'MINIMAX_API_KEY'}
  ...
```

`opencode config` (and `opencode debug config`) shows `"disabled_providers": ["minimax", "minimax-cn"]` in the resolved config, yet `provider.list` still includes the four MiniMax entries.

### Workaround that works for me

Unset the env var (or remove the `export` line from `~/.bashrc`) and restart opencode. With the env var gone, the providers are no longer auto-enabled, and the model selector stops listing them:

```bash
unset MINIMAX_API_KEY MINIMAX_API_BASE
```

Keeping `disabled_providers` in `opencode.json` is still a good idea as a belt-and-suspenders measure for when the env var is set.

### Recommendation

Two follow-ups worth opening as separate issues:

1. **`auth logout` should not leave providers in a zombie state.** When the user explicitly removes a credential, the env-var auto-loading should also be disabled, or at minimum the user should be warned that the provider will be re-enabled on next launch. Currently the only way to be sure a provider is gone is to track down every place the env var is set.
2. **`disabled_providers` is not honored by the TUI.** `CatalogV2.provider.available()` should apply the same `isProviderAllowed` check that the runtime loader uses, so user intent expressed in the config file is respected everywhere.

Closing this as not-a-bug on the original report, but the env-var behavior is surprising enough to deserve a UX improvement. Sorry for the noise.
